foot_p: Games for learning, made in Brazil by Eduardo Silva.
fot_l1: A photon that takes two paths at once
fot_l2: Interference, measurement and the bomb found without touching it
fot_l4: 42 levels in 9 chapters, no formulas, ages 8+
fot_p: Drag mirrors, beam splitters, filters and detectors, and fire photons one at a time. The rules are a real quantum simulation: you see the phenomenon before you read the explanation.
fot_tag: Mirror-and-light puzzles that teach real quantum physics.
harpa_p: The 640 hymns of the Harpa Cristã (a Brazilian Christian hymnal), with lyrics search, lists and dark mode. No ads and fully offline. Portuguese only.
hero_p: Fly a rocket through Earth's real gravity. Guide light through mirrors and watch quantum physics happen. Combine chemical elements to defeat the Rust. For students, teachers and the curious.

orb_alt2: alt="Animated hint showing the right maneuver"

orb_l1: Why an orbit is a fall that never reaches the ground
orb_l3: A Moon rendezvous and a trip to Mars with the Hohmann transfer
orb_l4: 23 stages, from training to an expedition across the solar system
orb_p: You control the engine and the direction of a rocket that obeys Earth's real gravity. No rails: the trajectory line shows, live, where it is going.
orb_tag: Fly a rocket and discover how orbits really work.
per_cap1: Choosing the team on the periodic table
per_cap2: Battle: the villain announces its move and you decide whether to dodge
per_l1: 40 real chemical reactions, each with a recorded source (IUPAC, PubChem, NIST and general chemistry textbooks)
per_l2: The periodic table is the team-selection screen: group, period and atomic number show up as you play
per_l3: Real properties become strategy: aluminum protects itself with a layer of alumina, and chromium and nickel resist corrosion
per_l4: 4 islands and 20 levels: Metals, Salts, Acids and Bases, and Alloys, with a boss at the end of each island
per_p: Build a team of three elements and face villains like the Rust in turn-based battles. To attack, combine two heroes: if the reaction really exists, it happens on screen with the real, balanced equation. If the combination has no source yet, the game says so instead of inventing chemistry.
per_tag: A chemistry RPG where the heroes are elements of the periodic table.
talk_p: Questions, suggestions, a bug you found in a game or an idea for using it in class. We reply to the email you give us.
teach_p1: The games use real laws, values and reactions. Where something is simplified to fit the game, the game itself says so, without pretending.
teach_p2: Just install and play. Progress stays on the student's device; no account data is requested.
teach_p3: Everything runs without internet. Some games show an ad now and then, always between levels and never in the middle of play.
teach_p4: The games explain the phenomenon but never teach lab procedures. Dangerous reactions come with a warning.
